name: Churchteams
shortDescription: A church management suite with groups, check-in, giving, workflows, volunteers, communications and a member app.
suitableContexts: Churches wanting a full-access trial with their own data
Teams that need groups, check-in and communications together

pricing.summary: Churchteams prices its plans by database people count. The current page publishes the plan structure, included essentials and 30-day trial, but does not display the subscription amounts; ask the supplier for a current quote.

tiers.label: Database-based plans
tiers.detail: Plan selection is based on people in the database

tiers.label: Text-to-Church
tiers.detail: 500 outgoing texts included; further texts are 2¢ each unless a bulk package is used

pricing.trialDetails: 30 days, full access and support, with the option to load the church’s own data according to the supplier.

importExport: Data import is free for small or less complex data according to the supplier

editorial.assessment: Churchteams offers a genuinely practical evaluation route because it says the full system, support and a church’s own data can be used during its 30-day trial. A UK church should still ask about payment, Gift Aid, currency, data-processing and total text-message cost.
bestFor: Teams that want to test a complete church-management environment
Churches with active group, check-in and volunteer workflows
limitations: The public pricing page does not display current subscription amounts; ask for a quote
Ask the supplier about UK finance and data arrangements

procurementVerdict.problem: Teams that want to test a complete church-management environment
procurementVerdict.firstCheck: Ask for the subscription price at the church's expected database size

longForm.verdict: Churchteams is most useful to assess as an operational workflow platform, not just a contact database. Its trial is strong enough to test a real group, volunteer or check-in process before a decision.

decisionLens.heading: A full-access trial is only useful with a defined exit and data plan.
decisionLens.text: The supplier says a church can load its own data during a trial. Decide in advance what is safe to import, who can access it, what success looks like and how the church will remove or retain data if it does not proceed.

sections.heading: Testing shared ministry workflows
sections.question: Can volunteers and administrators use the same system without creating side lists?
paragraphs: Churchteams lists groups, communication, giving, volunteers, registration, check-in and workflows among its essentials.
Use the 30-day trial to set permissions, run a check-in or registration, schedule a volunteer and test the communications and exports that a team actually needs.

userFeedback.summary: This profile does not use supplier testimonials or review material as an independent score. It is based on the supplier’s plan and trial information.
themes: The full-access trial can test actual team hand-offs.
Text-message costs and imported-data scope need explicit review.
userFeedback.caveat: No conclusion about user satisfaction or UK suitability should be inferred from this limited source record.

faq.question: Does Churchteams offer a free trial?
faq.answer: Yes. Churchteams advertises a 30-day trial with full system access, support and the option to load a church’s own data.

faq.question: How is Churchteams priced?
faq.answer: Churchteams says its plans are based on people in the database. Check the current price and any complex-data import charge directly with the supplier.

faq.question: Does Churchteams support UK Gift Aid?
faq.answer: Ask the supplier to demonstrate UK payment methods, Gift Aid workflow, finance exports and data-processing terms before adoption.

seo.title: Churchteams review for UK churches
seo.description: Independent Churchteams profile for UK churches: 30-day trial, pricing structure, core features, key checks and FAQs.
